svg.text: The Cyborg: why he reads as generic, and six directions
Orb: the Cyborg looks generic and is the least compelling of the launch fighters; focus here first. Each direction shows the silhouette at fight size (colour, then flat black at 120 and 40 px), and
the face at cut-in size (neutral and hurt). Working labels, pending Legal review. Orb picks, or mixes.
his face today: neutral and hurt
the four fighters flat black at 80 px: three have a hook, one is a box
A rectangle on a rectangle: a box head on a wide box torso. His extras (a backpack, a mail apron) are small and sit inside the outline, so flat black
at 40 px he is a block with arms. The others each have a shape that sticks out (a tuft, a tail, a topknot and mantle).
He has none: a display box. The close-up work gave him the half-human, half-metal face with one lit eye, which is the most common cyborg face there
Dark maroon plating, dark limbs, grey gear, a coral accent: the stock dark-armoured soldier, and dark on dark so the figure has no value structure.
The others each have one clear light and one clear dark.
The stair of squares says "digital", which every robot says. It is not tied to what he does, how he moves or who he is.
Nothing says what kind of person or machine he is, or how he fights. The Protagonist is bright and open, the Anti-hero is a cold slash, the Empress is
a regal wedge. He is a heavy soldier.
as a person, not a robot
Bolder: a person in a machine

For Orb: what to look at

Three directions keep him recognisably the same fighter (1 Stepper, 2 Stack, 5 Prosthetic: heavy, boxy, stepped, the dark red lane). 3 Furnace is a heavier cousin; 4 Frame and 6 Sprinter change what he is. Questions: is he a heavy

brawler, a person in a machine, or something quicker and stranger? Which one hook (a staircase, sliding blocks, vents, a window chest, one huge arm, blade legs) do you want to see on the screen at 40 px? Any two can be combined
(for example the Stepper's staircase on the Prosthetic's lopsided build).

Rules kept: every lit part is the pale cream-peach tone (never saturated coral, no lone red eye); no bolts, no stitches, no goggles, no gold, no spiky hair; no franchise names or looks. Screening notes are under each direction.
